affected_system: roadway, bridge, sidewalk, signal, and public right-of-way asset network
alternatives: protect minimum coverage before needs-based allocation of road and bridge maintenance resources
adapt allocations using observed demand, uptake, and capacity for road and bridge maintenance resources
pair risk-, skill-, network-, and minimum-service allocation with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Assets, inspections, defects, work orders, costs, traffic, restrictions, and completion are reconciled.
Engineering thresholds and deterioration models are locally reviewed and versioned.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: retain the current distribution rule for road and bridge maintenance resources.

constraints.description: The road and bridge asset management allocate must respect declared minimum service, eligibility, capacity, and distributional safeguards.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: public works asset manager and chief infrastructure engineer
decision_question: How should qualified crews, specialty equipment, materials, and inspection capacity be assigned?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The road and bridge asset management allocate must respect declared minimum service, eligibility, capacity, and distributional safeguards.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for road and bridge maintenance resources passes documented checks for eligible denominators, group attributes, inventory, minimum-service rules, and allocation records.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: risk-, skill-, network-, and minimum-service allocation
independence_key.primary_outcome: high-consequence work without assigned qualified capacity

intended_claim: A versioned allocate design for comparing declared alternatives affecting road and bridge maintenance resources, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: high-consequence work without assigned qualified capacity
distributional gap in high-consequence work without assigned qualified capacity
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not report assigned resources as inspected, repaired, reopened, or safe assets.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for road and bridge maintenance resources passes documented checks for eligible denominators, group attributes, inventory, minimum-service rules, and allocation records.

title: Allocate maintenance crews, equipment, and materials
transportability_risks: Materials, climate, loading, standards, inspection, procurement, and unit costs differ.
Service requests can reveal workload but not structural condition or safety.
